claims.text: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy undergoes a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
The baseline alloy forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during cooling.
Increasing the phosphorus content will suppress primary non-eutectic crystalline-phase formation during rapid cooling.
Increasing the phosphorus content will improve the thermal stability of the retained amorphous phase during reheating.
The intervention substitutes a small fraction of the transition-metal content with additional phosphorus.
Rapid melt spinning can provide cooling rates above approximately 10^5 K/s for the proposed treatment.
Additional phosphorus disrupts regular atomic packing.
The packing disruption destabilizes nucleation sites for primary crystalline phases.
Added phosphorus increases local chemical heterogeneity in the undercooled melt.
The increased chemical heterogeneity raises the critical nucleation barrier.
Reduced atomic mobility inhibits the growth of primary crystalline phases during rapid cooling.
The phosphorus-enriched alloy will retain a higher amorphous-phase fraction after rapid cooling than the baseline alloy.
The phosphorus-enriched alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature during reheating than the baseline alloy.
The predicted benefit is expected at cooling rates above approximately 10^5 K/s.
Much slower cooling may eliminate the predicted benefit.
Reheating significantly above the crystallization-onset temperature may eliminate the predicted benefit.

contradictions.description: The notation Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20+x implies adding phosphorus without reducing the listed transition-metal amounts, whereas the intervention says phosphorus substitutes for a fraction of the transition metals. The modified composition is therefore not defined consistently or normalized.

The stated reheating condition requires remaining below Tx, but determining Tx by DSC requires heating through the crystallization onset. The proposed test therefore necessarily crosses a boundary that the processing description says should not be crossed.
